title: Signature declares `alg: none` against a published public key set
rationale: Relabelled from `violating` to `undecidable` on 30 July 2026, after the primary text was read. Verification is never attempted here rather than attempted and passed: a signature made under `none`, or under a symmetric algorithm whose key the operator publishes, is evidence of nothing, because anyone holding the published material can produce it, and crediting it would inflate the paper's cryptographic-binding number with endpoints that have no binding at all. But declining to credit a signature and convicting its publisher are separate acts, and only the second needs a MUST that binds the publisher. There is none: RFC 7518 3.6's obligations are addressed to the verifier, and RFC 8725 -- which does prohibit this -- is a BCP about JWTs, while an A2A agent-card signature is a detached JWS over a JCS-canonicalised card with no claims set. BCP 195, cited alongside RFC 7518 in every C15 verdict until this date, is a TLS document and was simply the wrong reference. C15 keeps its MUST for the one condition that has one -- RSA below 2048 bits, RFC 7518 3.3 -- which `c15-violating-rsa-key-below-2048-bits` now covers. C04 becomes UNSPECIFIED here for the same reason: reporting that the signature failed to verify would be a false statement about a signature nobody tested.
key_provenance: Nothing here is signed, which is the point: the protected header base64url-decodes to {"alg": "none", "kid": "agent-example-key-1", "jku": "https://agent.example.org/.well-known/jwks.json"} and the signature is deliberately the empty octet sequence. The key set served below is the same published P-256 public key as in `c03-c04-c15-conforming-signed-card-verifies`, so the key resolves and only the algorithm differs between the two fixtures.

spec.quote: Implementations that support Unsecured JWSs MUST NOT accept such objects as valid unless the application specifies that it is acceptable for a specific object to not be integrity protected.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026. Read closely, this is the sentence that DEMOTED C15's `none` condition rather than anchoring it: every MUST in 3.6 binds an implementation *accepting* a JWS, not one publishing it. Nothing in RFC 7518 forbids a publisher from emitting `alg: none`.

spec.quote: The goal of this document is to facilitate secure implementation and deployment of JWTs.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified 30 July 2026. Recorded because it is the document that WOULD have anchored a MUST here and does not reach: its subject is JWTs, and an agent-card signature is a detached JWS over a JCS payload. This closes the question left open in the earlier version of this fixture.

spec.quote: A key of size 2048 bits or larger MUST be used with these algorithms.
spec.verification: verbatim-verified against rfc-editor.org, 30 July 2026. Included here to record what C15 retained: this is the only condition of the three with a MUST binding the party the instrument observes.
